teachingQuestion: How do secure design principles reduce a single failure’s impact?
focalInsight: Layers should address different trust boundaries and failure paths while least privilege and safe defaults limit blast radius at every layer.
title: Design layers around one protected action
caption: No one layer is sufficient; each narrows a different path to unauthorized action or unsafe failure.

nodes.label: Service boundary
nodes.detail: Minimal service privilege and secure defaults

nodes.label: Data boundary
nodes.detail: Scoped access, integrity, encryption as required

nodes.label: Failure response
nodes.detail: Deny or limit unsafe action and alert owner

altSummary: A five-layer stack separates request validation, minimally privileged service behavior, data protection, controlled operations, and safe failure response.
textFallback: At the request boundary, validate identity, input, and authorization. The service runs with minimal privilege and safe defaults. The data boundary scopes access and applies integrity or encryption needs. Operations is separated and monitored. When a critical security dependency fails, the system denies or limits unsafe actions and alerts an accountable responder.
